claims.text: Adding TiC nanoparticles to a refractory high-entropy alloy can enhance its high-temperature mechanical performance.
Adding TiC nanoparticles can enhance the mechanical performance of a refractory high-entropy alloy under irradiation.
A TiC-containing refractory high-entropy alloy can maintain thermal stability.
A TiC-containing refractory high-entropy alloy can maintain irradiation stability.
The proposed intervention is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys in either an as-cast or wrought state.
The proposed performance benefit should hold above 800 °C.
TiC nanoparticles act as pinning sites for dislocations.
TiC nanoparticles act as pinning sites for grain boundaries.
Pinning dislocations and grain boundaries with TiC nanoparticles increases resistance to high-temperature deformation.
Pinning dislocations and grain boundaries with TiC nanoparticles increases resistance to deformation under irradiation.
TiC nanoparticle pinning can strengthen the alloy without compromising thermal stability.
TiC nanoparticle pinning can strengthen the alloy without compromising irradiation stability.
Relative to an otherwise comparable RHEA without TiC nanoparticles, the TiC-containing RHEA will have improved yield strength at high temperature and under irradiation.
Relative to an otherwise comparable RHEA without TiC nanoparticles, the TiC-containing RHEA will have improved ductility at high temperature and under irradiation.
A TiC concentration between 0.5 and 2.0 vol% is proposed as the intervention range.
A TiC particle-size range between 10 and 50 nm is proposed.
